glassbox-canonical 1
version 2
id "itajara-loop"
title "One loop of the Itajara looper daemon"
clock -
initial "empty"
notes 112
  note "The phase machine of one loop in the Itajara daemon (music/itajara/daemon/"
  note "src/engine.rs), written down. The daemon runs six u8 constants — IDLE,"
  note "ARMED, FIRST, OVERDUB, PLAYING, MULTIPLY — set at seventeen sites from three"
  note "threads, and what each byte MEANS depends on flags beside it: `threaded`,"
  note "`one_pass`, `close_at`/`rec_len`, `request`/`request_at`, `level_arm`/"
  note "`arm_from`. This artifact is that byte and those flags as one machine, so"
  note "the daemon's Rust and the pedalboard's PureScript can be held to the same"
  note "table instead of agreeing by care. It is prescriptive in a few places, and"
  note "each is named below; loop.json next door is untouched and is a witness."
  note ""
  note "WHICH QUALIFIERS BECAME STATES. The test used: a qualifier is a state when"
  note "it changes what the host must do on ENTRY or what more than one event does;"
  note "it is a fact when only a guard reads it at the moment of a press. So:"
  note ""
  note "  * Armed splits in three. Listening for a sound (`lev1`) and waiting for"
  note "    the bar line (`g1` on an empty loop) enter differently — one claims the"
  note "    input and watches it, the other files a request the output callback"
  note "    will honour — and a second press cancels the first but is a no-op on"
  note "    the second. The daemon spells the first as ARMED and the second as"
  note "    IDLE-with-a-request; here both are states, because both are 'about to"
  note "    record' and neither is idle. The third is both at once: a listening"
  note "    loop whose sound has been found while quantise is on files a request"
  note "    for the bar and KEEPS the input — `armed-by-sound`. It is not"
  note "    `armed-for-grid`, and the replay of 2026-09-06 (step 5b) is what said"
  note "    so: a second press cancels it, and an outage drops the request and"
  note "    leaves it listening, where `armed-for-grid` shrugs off the press and"
  note "    an outage returns it to rest. Only an empty or sized loop ever waits"
  note "    for the bar without a sound — a pressed overdub starts on the press —"
  note "    so `armed-for-grid`'s exits read `has-length` alone."
  note "  * Recording splits by whether it closes itself. A first take with a"
  note "    known length (`fix`, `len`, or a length kept from before) arms"
  note "    `close_at` on entry and the closer thread delivers `closed`; an open"
  note "    take waits for the foot. Same for an overdub: one pass arms its close,"
  note "    an ordinary overdub does not. Four recording states, two entry lists."
  note "  * Empty, Sized and Tape are three rest states, not one with facts. They"
  note "    answer `record` differently (an open first take, a sized first take, an"
  note "    overdub), `blank` differently (allowed, allowed, re-thread) and enter"
  note "    differently (wipe, nothing, thread a silent layer). `threaded` was a"
  note "    flag; here it is where you are."
  note "  * Multiply is its own state, as it is in the daemon."
  note ""
  note "WHICH QUALIFIERS STAYED FACTS. `level-arm`, `quantised` and `one-pass` are"
  note "modes a verb toggles between presses; the machine reads them when `record`"
  note "arrives and never carries them. `writable`, `plain`, `at-ceiling` and"
  note "`input-held-elsewhere` are the daemon's own guards (`not_writable`,"
  note "`not_plain`, the layer ceiling, `busy_elsewhere`), asked in the daemon's"
  note "order so the same press gets the same refusal. `has-length`, `has-layers`"
  note "and `threaded` are read in exactly one place: on the way OUT of an armed"
  note "state, to know where a cancelled arm returns to and what kind of take a"
  note "found sound begins. That is the history-state problem the README names,"
  note "and this is its documented workaround — the host holds the memory and the"
  note "machine asks for it. `last-layer` tells `undo` whether it has just made"
  note "the loop Sized. `has-grid` is what `len` needs before a bar means anything."
  note ""
  note "WHAT IS CONFIG. `fixed-rig` (`--fixed` at launch) is the one thing that"
  note "reshapes the diagram: on a fixed rig `clear` lands on Tape, not Empty, so"
  note "every slot is an empty tape of one length. The initial state is Empty"
  note "regardless; a fixed rig seeds each slot with `Drive.enter tape`, which is"
  note "what `enter` is for."
  note ""
  note "WHY THERE ARE NO DEADLINES. A sized take closes itself after ITS OWN"
  note "LENGTH in frames, which is neither config nor a literal — it is the host's"
  note "memory. `after` cannot say that, so the close is a runtime event `closed`,"
  note "and `arm-close` on entry is the command that tells the host to schedule"
  note "it. The closer thread and the callback keep the timing; the machine keeps"
  note "only that a close is owed. With no deadlines the machine declares no"
  note "clock, and `Host.reportClock` accepts it on a host with no timer at all."
  note ""
  note "COMMANDS. Every recording state establishes itself on entry (zero the"
  note "layer, stamp the origin, start the write; arm the close if it knows its"
  note "length) and commits on exit (`close-take` for a first take, whose length"
  note "becomes the cycle; `close-layer` for an overdub; `close-multiply`, which"
  note "rounds to cycles and grows the loop). Exit commands are used here against"
  note "the README's advice, and knowingly: the commit is the one thing every way"
  note "OUT of a recording owes, including `clear` and a lost device. On those two"
  note "exits the host's `close-take` has less to commit than usual — nothing,"
  note "after an outage with a hole in it — and it knows that, because it is the"
  note "thing that raised `lost`. The armed states also pay on exit:"
  note "`release-input` gives the converter back and `cancel-request` withdraws a"
  note "request the callback has not consumed; both are harmless after the take"
  note "actually began, because `start-take` consumes what they would clear."
  note ""
  note "WHAT THE MACHINE DOES NOT KNOW. Arguments. `fix13` stores thirteen seconds,"
  note "`len4` stores four bars, `blank13` threads thirteen seconds: the number is"
  note "the verb's, the phase change is the machine's, and the host keeps the"
  note "number the way it keeps every count. The same goes for `undo` on a loop"
  note "with layers to spare (a layer goes; the phase does not), for `fix` on a"
  note "loop with material (it sets `one-pass`, a fact), and for `len` on a loop"
  note "with material (it declares or resizes; the phase does not move — but it"
  note "asks for a bar first, as it does on an empty loop, unless the loop is"
  note "itself the bar, which is `has-grid` too; the replay found this)."
  note ""
  note "WHERE THIS IS PRESCRIPTIVE. The daemon does not guard `u`, `x`, `z` or"
  note "`blank` against an armed loop, and does not guard `u` or `z` against a"
  note "recording one; a press there would decrement a layer under a live write"
  note "or forget a length mid-take. Here every one of them refuses"
  note "`still-recording`, which is the tag `fix` already uses for the same case."
  note "The daemon also lets `x` on an armed loop abandon the arm and start a"
  note "multiply; here it refuses. Adopting this artifact makes those refusals"
  note "real, and that is intended. ADOPTED 2026-09-06 (step 5b): the daemon"
  note "guards every one of them now (`guards::still_recording`), a cancelled"
  note "arm returns to what the loop held rather than to idle, and"
  note "`daemon/src/engine/conformance.rs` replays this machine's vectors"
  note "through the engine — so this table is what the daemon is tested"
  note "against, not a description of it."
  note ""
  note "REFUSAL TAGS are the daemon's acks: `input-held` ('loop N has the input'),"
  note "`not-writable` (swinging, or a tape at speed), `not-plain` ('playing at"
  note "xN; sp1 to record into it'), `at-ceiling`, `still-recording` ('finish"
  note "that first'), `nothing-to-undo`, `nothing-to-multiply`, `has-material`"
  note "('has something in it' / 'layers still playing'), `no-length` ('no length"
  note "set'), `no-grid` ('no bar yet')."
states 12
  state "armed-by-level" "Listening for a sound" false (entry 1 "listen") (exit 1 "release-input")
  state "armed-by-sound" "Sound found, waiting for the bar" false (entry 1 "request-at-boundary") (exit 2 "release-input" "cancel-request")
  state "armed-for-grid" "Waiting for the bar" false (entry 1 "request-at-boundary") (exit 1 "cancel-request")
  state "empty" "Empty" false (entry 1 "wipe") (exit 0)
  state "multiplying" "Multiplying" false (entry 1 "start-multiply") (exit 1 "close-multiply")
  state "overdubbing-one-pass" "Overdubbing, one pass" false (entry 2 "start-layer" "arm-close") (exit 1 "close-layer")
  state "overdubbing-open" "Overdubbing" false (entry 1 "start-layer") (exit 1 "close-layer")
  state "playing" "Playing" false (entry 0) (exit 0)
  state "recording-open" "Recording, open" false (entry 1 "start-take") (exit 1 "close-take")
  state "recording-sized" "Recording, sized" false (entry 2 "start-take" "arm-close") (exit 1 "close-take")
  state "sized" "Sized, empty" false (entry 0) (exit 0)
  state "tape" "Threaded tape" false (entry 1 "thread-tape") (exit 0)
events 13
  event "blank" "thread a tape (blank)" user
  event "boundary" "the bar line arrived" runtime
  event "clear" "clear (c)" user
  event "closed" "the take reached its length" runtime
  event "fix" "fix the next take (fix)" user
  event "free" "forget the length (z)" user
  event "level-off" "level-arm off (lev0)" user
  event "lost" "the audio device was lost" runtime
  event "multiply" "multiply (x)" user
  event "record" "record (r)" user
  event "size" "size in bars (len)" user
  event "sound" "a sound crossed the threshold" runtime
  event "undo" "undo (u)" user
config 1
  config "fixed-rig" "Every slot is a tape of one fixed length (--fixed)" (bool false)
facts 12
  fact "at-ceiling" "The loop is at the layer ceiling"
  fact "has-grid" "A bar exists: Link is running or a loop has a length"
  fact "has-layers" "The loop has at least one layer"
  fact "has-length" "The loop has a length"
  fact "input-held-elsewhere" "Another loop holds the converter"
  fact "last-layer" "Only one layer is left"
  fact "level-arm" "Level-arm is on: wait for a sound rather than the press"
  fact "one-pass" "The next layer is one pass and closes itself"
  fact "plain" "Playing plainly: x1, forwards"
  fact "quantised" "Quantise is on: start on the bar line"
  fact "threaded" "The loop was a threaded tape"
  fact "writable" "The write head can follow the play head: not swinging, not a tape at speed"
refusals 10
  refusal "at-ceiling" "the loop is at the layer ceiling; undo one first"
  refusal "has-material" "the loop has something in it; undo or clear it first"
  refusal "input-held" "another loop has the input; one converter, one recording — finish that first"
  refusal "no-grid" "no bar yet: there is no clock and no loop has a length"
  refusal "no-length" "no length is set; the next recording sets one"
  refusal "not-plain" "the loop is playing at a speed; sp1 to record into it"
  refusal "not-writable" "a write head cannot follow this play head: put the speed back, or stop the pendulum"
  refusal "nothing-to-multiply" "the loop has nothing to multiply; record a loop first"
  refusal "nothing-to-undo" "the loop has nothing to undo"
  refusal "still-recording" "the loop is recording; finish that first"
commands 13
  command "arm-close" "Set close_at one length on; the closer delivers `closed`"
  command "cancel-request" "Withdraw a pending request"
  command "close-layer" "Commit the layer: shape it, draw it, count it"
  command "close-multiply" "Round to whole cycles and grow the loop to fit"
  command "close-take" "Commit the first take: its length becomes the cycle, draw the layer"
  command "listen" "Claim the input and watch it for the threshold"
  command "release-input" "Give the input back; no take began"
  command "request-at-boundary" "Ask the output callback to start the take on the next bar line"
  command "start-layer" "Zero the next layer, record from origin, start the modular write"
  command "start-multiply" "Zero the next layer and record from the top of this cycle"
  command "start-take" "Zero layer 0, stamp origin and rec_from, start the linear write"
  command "thread-tape" "Lay down a silent layer of the asked-for length, going round"
  command "wipe" "Zero every layer and forget the length"
